node/adapter/src/lib.rs.review: Both copies declare SLOT_ANCHOR_ACTIVATION_ID, the feature that enables NPOOL004 pools, with the same bytes; the five identifiers, the program id and the compute charge are equal. Without behaviour: the workspace takes the program id and the pool address from native_accounts (same bytes, same seed) and adds prepare_verifying_key, which builds the verifying key before the first payment instead of during it.

node/adapter/src/nullifiers.rs.review: The workspace derives the marker address through native_accounts::nullifier_address: same seeds, same program id, same result.

node/adapter/src/processor.rs.review: Finalization lives in processor/finalization.rs in the workspace. What remains here is the candidate copy's entry rules in the same order with the same errors: the opcode, the charge of compute units, the top-level check, the slot, the two finalizing opcodes and the staging instructions. Without behaviour: the workspace reaches the compute meter and the Clock sysvar through processor/runtime_features.rs where the candidate copy names its runtime's interfaces; process asks for the state of the slot-anchor feature once and hands it to process_gated, where the candidate copy reads it at the check; prepare_verifying_key and its test; the declarations of two test modules. More lines differ than before the workspace had the slot-anchor rule, because the workspace text now names its binding functions; the difference in what the two programs do is recorded for processor/runtime_features.rs.

node/adapter/src/staging.rs.review: The workspace wraps native_accounts::Buffer, which holds the candidate copy's Buffer line for line, and maps its two errors to the same two instruction errors.

protocol/payments/src/envelope.rs.review: The workspace derives Debug on DecodedEnvelope. No other line differs; encoding and every check are the same text.

protocol/payments/src/lib.rs.review: The workspace declares the native_accounts module, which the candidate series does not have. The error type and every other line are the same text.

protocol/payments/src/state.rs.review: The workspace has two rules that the candidate copy lacks: with_payment refuses a payment in which either note is the empty leaf, and decode refuses an NPOOL004 state whose tree the next completed slot could not record (notes under the root of the empty tree, or a root that a stored checkpoint holds for another note count). The candidate copy applies such a payment and decodes such a state. The patch recorded under proposed_patches makes the same change to the candidate copy; with it applied the two files differ in 7 and 186 lines, as they did before the rules were added. The rest is the earlier review, unchanged: The workspace adds PoolState::complete_slot, which records a slot checkpoint in place and reuses the newest checkpoint's root while the note count is unchanged; the candidate copy recomputes the root from the frontier for every slot. decode refuses a newest checkpoint whose root is not the frontier root at the same count, and only with_payment changes the frontier, so both give the same bytes for every reachable state. The cost differs: the candidate copy hashes 32 tree levels and copies the state for every completed slot. Also: Debug on PoolState, four more tests, import order and one assertion's layout; with the two rules, one more test, and one test that pays in ordinary notes where the candidate copy's pays in empty leaves.

protocol/payments/src/wire.rs.review: The workspace makes the three tags and two size constants public with doc comments and derives Debug on DecodedPayment. encode and decode are the same text.

node/adapter/src/processor/finalization..review: The workspace's finalization, split out of processor.rs into four helpers. Every check and effect is the candidate copy's, in the same order with the same errors, including the refusal of an NPOOL004 pool while the slot-anchor feature is inactive and the accepted anchors taken from PoolState::accepted_roots(slot). Without behaviour: the state of the feature is a parameter; rent and the System program are reached through processor/runtime_features.rs; the allocation and assignment of a marker name the marker's address and its nullifier, where the candidate copy builds the seeds of the same address.

node/adapter/src/processor/runtime_featu.review: The workspace program's binding to the Agave 3.0.14 runtime: five functions for what the candidate copy writes in the words of the 4.3.2 runtime. Four pass their arguments on and return the runtime's answer: the compute meter, the sysvar cache, an invocation with no added signer, and an invocation signed for a marker's address, where the candidate copy passes the seeds of that address. The fifth is a difference in behaviour: slot_anchors answers false always, because the 3.0.14 feature set has no native_slot_anchors switch. The program built from the workspace therefore refuses every NPOOL004 pool, as the candidate copy does while the feature is inactive, and can never accept one; the candidate copy reads the switch from its runtime.

Tests only, compiled for test builds: the compute units charged, the slot and the rent read, and the System program invocations of the registered program, in the mock context of the 3.0.14 runtime. No counterpart in the candidate series, whose program tests are in its harness crate.

node/adapter/src/processor/slot_anchor_t.review: Tests only, compiled for test builds: the slot-anchor rule run through the finalizer with real proofs, with the state of the feature given by the test and the end of a slot performed by the test. No counterpart in the candidate series, whose tests of the rule are in its harness crate.

protocol/payments/src/native_accounts.rs.review: Program id, pool and marker address derivation and the staging buffer, moved here from the adapter so that wallets can use them without the validator. The candidate series keeps the same code in adapter/src/lib.rs, nullifiers.rs and staging.rs.

node/candidate/drafts/pool-state-hardeni.review: A proposal: outside the reconstruction plan and not built with the candidate toolchain. It changes zolana-native/protocol/src/state.rs only and adds the two pool-state rules recorded for protocol/payments/src/state.rs. The README beside it gives the file's identity before and after. When it joins the plan, delete this entry and review the state.rs record again.
